messages.author: 89a4640ddc6e46d0
messages.subject: Help: Implementing LKJ Approach for Covariance Matrix
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to implement the LKJ approach to estimate the mean vector and covariance matrix from a multivariate normal distribution. My understanding of the approach is basic, and I have mostly pieced it together from the STAN mailing lists. Any help would be appreciated.

I have attached a functioning example.

QUESTION 1.
The code runs, and I obtain reasonable estimates, however I get the following error
Informational Message: The parameter state is about to be Metropolis rejected due to the following underlying, non-fatal (really) issue (and please ignore that what comes next might say 'error'): Error in function stan::prob::lkj_cov_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Covariance matrix is 1.#INF:0, but must be finite!
If the problem persists across multiple draws, you might have a problem with an initial state or a gradient somewhere.
If the problem does not persist, the resulting samples will still be drawn from the posterior.
My prior on the standard deviation seems reasonable, and eta is 1... so I am not sure why I am getting this error. Is my parameterization incorrect?

QUESTION 2.
 Are there any guidelines on how to choose the value of eta?

Thank you,

Mark

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Help: Implementing LKJ Approach for Covariance Matrix
parts:
On Thursday, August 8, 2013 6:02:50 PM UTC-4, Markian Pahuta wrote:
I am trying to implement the LKJ approach to estimate the mean vector and covariance matrix from a multivariate normal distribution. My understanding of the approach is basic, and I have mostly pieced it together from the STAN mailing lists. Any help would be appreciated.

We regret having the lkj_cov density because it hard-codes a lognormal prior on the standard deviations. It is better to just put a lkj_corr prior on the correlation matrix and whatever prior you want on the standard deviations. But to answer your questions directly

QUESTION 1.
The code runs, and I obtain reasonable estimates, however I get the following error
Informational Message: The parameter state is about to be Metropolis rejected due to the following underlying, non-fatal (really) issue (and please ignore that what comes next might say 'error'): Error in function stan::prob::lkj_cov_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Covariance matrix is 1.#INF:0, but must be finite!
If the problem persists across multiple draws, you might have a problem with an initial state or a gradient somewhere.
If the problem does not persist, the resulting samples will still be drawn from the posterior.
If it just happens a small number of times toward the beginning, don't worry about it. Overflow happens and if so, proposals get rejected. Not a big deal.
My prior on the standard deviation seems reasonable, and eta is 1... so I am not sure why I am getting this error. Is my parameterization incorrect?

QUESTION 2.
 Are there any guidelines on how to choose the value of eta?

The manual has some explanation. Basically, eta is akin to the shape parameter of a beta distribution if both shape parameters are constrained to be equal (especially in the 2x2 case where there is only 1 free parameter in the correlation matrix). So

0 < eta < 1 -> U-shaped (i.e. correlation matrix has no mode)
eta == 1 -> uniform over the space of correlation matrices
1 < eta -> upside down U-shaped (i.e. correlation matrix as a mode at the identity)
As eta approaches infinity, the only correlation matrix with positive density is the identity.

Ben
